title: オブジェクト指向プログラミング
subtitle: Object Oriented Programming
teachers:
KAJI Shunpei
授業科目の学習・教育目標
educationalGoal: Learn object-oriented concepts, programming, and application development with the Java language. Programming corresponds to the implementation phase of the software development process. This course uses the learning results of 'Programming I', 'Programming II', and 'Programming III'. The results obtained from this course can be used in 'Software Design'.
advice:
In this course, students will learn about object-oriented development methods such as classes, inheritance, and encapsulation through learning object-oriented programming using Java language. They will also develop applications and understanding of practical Java functions.

Specific items are as follows.
1. Understand object-oriented concepts and features
2. Learn object-oriented programming notation using Java
3. Create applications using a package
4. Learn development methods through application development

Please note the following:
- Bring your own laptop computer.
- Try textbook examples and sample programs to see how they work.
- If there is a lack of programming or development tool operation skills, ensure enough review time.
books:
Java 第3版入門編　ゼロから始めるプログラミング　翔泳社(1年次後学期プログラミング科目で使用したもの）
Java 第3版実践編　アプリケーション作りの基本　翔泳社
requiredKnowledge:
The prerequisite skills for this course are the basics of the Java language and how to create a program.
Review the second half of 'Programming II (Java language basics) as it will be the prerequisite knowledge for this course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to understand object-oriented terms, Java language notation, and API specifications.
Be able to understand and explain object-oriented concepts such as classes, inheritance, and polymorphism.
Be able to write classes, instances, encapsulation, inheritance, and polymorphism in the Java language.
Be able to create applications using packages and explain development methods.

achievementLevels.ideal:
In addition to standard achievement goals, the following are required:

4) Be able to create a Java program that considers performance, readability, and efficiency.
5) Be able to explain the program outline, functions, class division, relation between classes, and instances, from the required specifications.
achievementLevels.standard:
The following three goals can be achieved:

1) Be able to explain the terms used in object-oriented programming.
2) Be able to perform learned object-oriented programming.
3) Be able to search for information on Java functions and packages required for Java application development.
